metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

AC item 'Version bump commit landed on main through Gerrit (change number and merge SHA r' cites operational evidence (merge_gate) that lives outside the codebase; tag it [non-codebase] — prefix the checkbox text with [non-codebase] so the completion verifier accepts a recorded attestation instead of failing to find code proof.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC proving the bug fix ships in v0.15.1 (e.g. `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-SHA> v0.15.1` plus a check that the installed 0.15.1 wheel omits `temperature` for an affected model id).
evidence: Context: 'needs to reach users ... a fix release containing that fix'
Approach: 'after the bug's fix has merged on main' — a precondition with no proving check
All six ACs assert version strings or artifact presence only
findings.finding: No acceptance criterion verifies that the published 0.15.1 actually contains the fix for bug tapestried-oversize-blackfly, which is the stated reason for the release. The ACs only prove that each channel reports version 0.15.1. Any 0.15.1 cut from a main that lacked the fix would satisfy every AC.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria / Approach preamble ('after the bug's fix has merged on main and the bug is closed')
scenarios: The release is cut from a worktree created before the fix merged.
The fix is reverted on main before the bump commit lands.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: '[non-codebase] Fix included: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tapestried-oversize-blackfly fix SHA> v0.15.1` exits 0 (SHA recorded in a comment). A smoke run of `rebar` plan review from `pip install nava-rebar==0.15.1` against one affected Bedrock model returns no 400.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC that `CHANGELOG.md` has a `## [0.15.1]` section with the sampling fix under Fixed and the RELEASE_DELTA/releases/fixVersions additions under Added, a `[0.15.1]` compare link, and that `git diff v0.15.0 -- tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json` shows only the `__version__` change.
evidence: Approach step 1: 'promote `## [Unreleased]` ... with hand-curated entries (the sampling fix under Fixed; releases/fixVersions under Added) and the compare footer link'
Approach step 1: '(only `__version__` changes in `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json`)'
Context: 'The CHANGELOG entry lists those additions so the patch number does not hide them' — this justification rests on an unverified deliverable
findings.finding: Two Scope deliverables have no covering acceptance criterion: (1) the hand-curated CHANGELOG entry (Fixed: sampling fix; Added: releases/fixVersions, plus the compare footer link); (2) the api_surface_baseline claim that 'only `__version__` changes'. The only AC on the bump commit is version-lockstep, which does not inspect either.
scenarios: The CHANGELOG ships without the Added section, so the SCHEMA_VERSION bump hidden behind a patch number goes undisclosed.
gen_api_surface reveals an unexpected public-API delta that gets silently committed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten the registry AC with `jq -e` on the exact server name with version 0.15.1 and latest status, and the Homebrew AC by decoding the formula and asserting the url contains `nava_rebar-0.15.1.tar.gz` and the sha256 equals the PyPI sdist digest.
evidence: 'curl -s "https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=io.github.navapbc/rebar"' lists version 0.15.1
'Formula/rebar.rb ... points at the 0.15.1 sdist (`gh api repos/navapbc/homebrew-rebar/contents/Formula/rebar.rb`)'
findings.finding: Two channel ACs use loose proving commands. The MCP Registry check uses a substring `search=` query and 'lists version 0.15.1', which a sibling server name or a non-latest entry could satisfy (taxonomy items 1 and 6). The Homebrew check reads base64 contents and says 'points at the 0.15.1 sdist' without asserting the URL or the sha256 against the PyPI sdist.
scenarios: The registry returns 0.15.1 for a different server, or 0.15.1 not flagged latest.
The formula URL is bumped but the sha256 is stale.
findings.suggested_fix: Registry: `curl -s ... | jq -e '.servers[] | select(.server.name=="io.github.navapbc/rebar" and .server.version=="0.15.1")'` (also checking the latest flag in `_meta`). Homebrew: `gh api repos/navapbc/homebrew-rebar/contents/Formula/rebar.rb -q .content | base64 -d | grep -E 'nava_rebar-0\.15\.1\.tar\.gz'`, and compare its sha256 to `curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/nava-rebar/0.15.1/json | jq -r '.urls[] | select(.packagetype=="sdist") | .digests.sha256'`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC proving the published 0.15.1 contains the tapestried-oversize-blackfly fix: record that the fix commit is an ancestor of the release commit, and/or that a `pip install nava-rebar==0.15.1` run against an affected model no longer sends `temperature` (no 400).
evidence: Context: 'needs to reach users ... a fix release containing that fix'
Approach: 'after the bug's fix has merged on main and the bug is closed' (precondition only, not an AC)
PyPI AC checks only `info.version` 0.15.1; GitHub/MCP/Homebrew ACs likewise check only version/artifact presence
Absence: no AC names the fix commit SHA as an ancestor of the release commit, nor exercises the fixed behavior from the published wheel
findings.finding: The plan's headline intent is to get the sampling fix for bug tapestried-oversize-blackfly to users. No acceptance criterion verifies that the released 0.15.1 artifact contains that fix. All channel ACs check only that a version string reads 0.15.1. 'After the bug's fix has merged on main and the bug is closed' is stated as a precondition in Approach but is never gated or evidenced. The release could therefore close green with the fix missing, for example if the cut happened before the fix merged or the fix was reverted.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (all items) vs. Context / Problem and Approach preamble
scenarios: Release is cut from a main that does not yet contain the fix (or the fix was reverted): every AC passes, yet users installing 0.15.1 still get 400s on Claude Opus/Sonnet 5 and other models that reject `temperature`.
An operator reviews the closed release ticket and cannot tell from the recorded evidence whether the fix shipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC along these lines: '[non-codebase] Fix shipped: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-SHA> v0.15.1` succeeds, and in a clean venv `pip install nava-rebar==0.15.1` followed by one plan-review/verifier call against a Claude Opus 5 (or other affected) Bedrock profile completes without the `temperature` 400.' Give it live-call provenance, and record the fix change number and the bug-closed state in the ticket comment.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before cutting the release, run 0.15.0 (`uvx nava-rebar==0.15.0`) against a store containing a RELEASE_DELTA event written by main and record that it reads and reduces without error; if it fails, bump to 0.16.0 instead.
evidence: '`SCHEMA_VERSION` 5→6 for the additive `RELEASE_DELTA` event (`src/rebar/reducer/_version.py`)'
'The event schema row says new event types are additive and preserved-and-ignored by older clients' — a cited doc claim, not an observed behavior
findings.finding: The plan asserts that the SCHEMA_VERSION 5→6 bump is safe for 0.15.0 clients, but the only basis cited is the docs' event-schema row. Nothing checks whether a 0.15.0 reducer tolerates a store or event stream stamped SCHEMA_VERSION 6, as opposed to refusing or erroring on a newer version. A patch release invites unattended upgrades on some machines but not others, such as Homebrew versus pip, so mixed-version clients on one repo are likely.
scenarios: A teammate on 0.15.0 reads a ticket store after another teammate on 0.15.1 writes a RELEASE_DELTA event.
The 0.15.0 reducer has a version guard that rejects schema > 5.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a back-out note: if 0.15.1 is defective, yank it on PyPI with a reason, revert the tap formula, and cut 0.15.2 via the same procedure (or cite the docs/releasing.md section that covers this).
evidence: Steps 3–5 describe forward publication only; there is no rollback, yank, or follow-up-release clause.
Acknowledgement alone is insufficient; a reversibility mechanism is required.
findings.finding: Publishing to PyPI, the GitHub Release, the MCP Registry and the Homebrew tap is irreversible: PyPI versions cannot be re-uploaded. The plan gives no back-out path if 0.15.1 turns out to be bad, such as a yank followed by a 0.15.2, a tap revert, or a registry status update.
scenarios: The wheel ships with a packaging defect or a regression from the 12 extra commits on main.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an Approach bullet: 'Back-out: `pip`-level yank of nava-rebar 0.15.1 via the PyPI UI or API with a reason; revert Formula/rebar.rb in navapbc/homebrew-rebar; mark the GitHub Release as not-latest; ship the fix as 0.15.2 by repeating this procedure.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the recovery for each non-Homebrew channel failure (e.g. re-run only the failed job via `gh run rerun $RUN --failed`; whether PyPI upload uses skip-existing), or cite the docs/releasing.md section that covers it.
evidence: Step 5: 'Confirm every channel; trigger ... autobump.yml ... if the tap has not bumped' — recovery is specified for Homebrew only
findings.finding: The plan does not handle a partially completed release in which some channels publish and others fail. Homebrew is the exception: step 5 says to trigger autobump. Missing is what to do if, for example, PyPI succeeds but the MCP Registry publish or the GitHub Release step fails, and whether re-running release.yml for the same version is idempotent.
scenarios: release.yml fails after PyPI upload; a re-run fails because the version already exists on PyPI.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In step 4, state how `$RUN` and the environment id are obtained (e.g. `RUN=$(gh run list --workflow release.yml --branch main --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')`; env id from `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/$RUN/pending_deployments -q '.[0].environment.id'`).
evidence: 'POST repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/$RUN/pending_deployments with a JSON `--input` body (`environment_ids` integer array)'
findings.finding: Step 4 uses `$RUN` and an `environment_ids` value but never says how to obtain them. `gh workflow run` does not print a run id. The step depends on state that no prior step establishes (taxonomy item 7).
scenarios: The executor picks the wrong run when several release.yml runs exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert before the POST: `RUN=$(gh run list --repo navapbc/rebar --workflow release.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')`; `ENV=$(gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/$RUN/pending_deployments -q '.[] | select(.environment.name=="pypi") | .environment.id')`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] List every user-facing change on main since v0.15.0 (`git log v0.15.0..origin/main`), including ADR 0123 plan_review_engine, the Claude 5.5 default-model change and the store-maintenance change. Re-check the patch-vs-minor rationale against the full list, and require the CHANGELOG to cover all of them, not just the sampling fix and releases.
evidence: Plan: "Main since v0.15.0 (12 commits) also carries the Jira-fixVersions \"releases\" feature (ADR 0124)" is the only listed non-fix content
Plan step 1: "hand-curated entries (the sampling fix under Fixed; releases/fixVersions under Added)"

CHANGELOG.md [0.15.1] as cut also lists 'ADR 0123: selectable plan-review engine, and the `[verify] plan_review_engine` setting' (Added), 'Configured default models move to the Claude 5.5 generation' (Changed), and the incremental-maintenance store change (Fixed). None of these is in the plan's list.
findings.finding: The patch-version rationale lists only part of what main contains. It names the Jira-fixVersions/releases feature (ADR 0124) as the only non-fix content since v0.15.0 and tells the CHANGELOG step to cover only 'the sampling fix under Fixed; releases/fixVersions under Added'. Main also carries at least three more user-facing changes: the ADR 0123 `[verify] plan_review_engine` config key, the default-model move to the Claude 5.5 generation, and the change from `gc --auto` to incremental git maintenance on store writes. The plan's claims that 'nothing on that page forces 0.16.0' and that the CHANGELOG keeps the patch number from hiding additions were judged without those three.
findings.location: Context / Problem (version rationale) and Approach step 1 (CHANGELOG curation)
scenarios: A user upgrading 0.15.0→0.15.1 expecting only fixes finds their configured default models have changed. That behavior change was never weighed in the patch-vs-minor decision.
An implementer following step 1 literally writes a CHANGELOG with only two items and leaves out the new config key and the model-default change.
findings.suggested_fix: In Context, replace the single-feature list with the full set of user-facing changes on main since v0.15.0 and say why each one is additive or a non-breaking behavior change. In Approach step 1, tell the curator to list every user-facing change under Fixed, Added or Changed, not only the sampling fix and releases.
